edits.headline: Farage-backed Stack BTC proposes £12m deal for a gold dealer
edits.subheadline: CoinDesk reported that the UK bitcoin treasury company would use the dealer's cash flow to buy more bitcoin.
editorialBody: Stack BTC, a UK bitcoin treasury company backed by Nigel Farage, has proposed buying precious metals dealer Direct Bullion for up to £12m ($16m), CoinDesk reported on 15 September.

The non-binding deal includes £3m in cash, about £4m in shares and £5m in performance-linked payments, CoinDesk reported. Stack plans to use the dealer's operating cash flow to support bitcoin purchases.
Farage's company, Thorn In The Side, invested £215,000 in Stack in March for about 6.3% of the company, according to CoinDesk.

A crypto tax package before the US House Ways and Means Committee leaves out a provision that would let miners and stakers defer tax on new tokens until they sell them, Cointelegraph reported. The committee was due to consider the 114-page bill, H.R. 10357, on 16 September.

Mobile armed units in Russia's border areas shoot down most Ukrainian drones flying deep into Russia, military expert Oleg Ivanov told TASS. He said the units use pickup trucks with crews of three or four and form a layered defence in the Kursk region.
People with student debt fall behind early when saving for retirement and do not catch up, MarketWatch reported.
A Russian warship fired flares at a Danish helicopter, DW News reported.
